sections.body:
A farm is a place where people grow food and keep animals. Some farms are full of plants, like rice fields and tea gardens. Other farms are full of animals, like cows, sheep and chickens. This is an animal farm, and it is a busy place from sunrise to sunset.

Every animal farm has the same few parts. There is the **barn**, a building where the animals sleep and where the hay is kept. There is the **yard**, an open space of ground where the animals walk about. There is the **field**, where the grass grows long and the animals eat. There is the **house**, where the farmer's family lives. And there is the **fence**, a line of posts and wire that keeps the animals in and keeps strangers out.

The animals have jobs, even if they do not know it. A cow gives milk. A hen gives eggs. A sheep gives wool. A horse pulls a cart. A dog watches the yard at night. A cat keeps the mice away from the grain. Even the bees have a job: they make honey, and they help the flowers grow fruit.

Most farm animals are gentle. They come when you call them, because they know the sound of your voice and the sound of a bucket. But they are still animals, and a frightened animal can push, bite or kick. So we ask children to keep their voices soft and to ask before they touch.

A farm is a good place to see how living things fit together. Grass feeds the cow. The cow feeds the farmer. The farmer feeds the hen. The hen gives us eggs for breakfast. Nothing on a farm is wasted, and every animal has its own part in the story.

By the end of this article you will know the animals you are likely to meet, the words farmers use for them, and how to visit a farm without upsetting anybody.
examples: This is a cow. She gives us milk.
The hens live in the shed and give us eggs.
May I feed the sheep, please?
sections.heading: What is a farm?

sections.body:
Cows eat grass all day and turn it into milk. Farmers milk them twice a day. A farmer can tell at once if a cow is not well, just by the way she walks.

Hens scratch the ground for seeds and small insects. A hen lays about one egg a day, and she likes to dust herself in dry soil to keep her feathers clean.

Sheep grow a soft coat of wool. The farmer shears it off in summer, and the sheep feels much cooler afterwards.

Goats are clever jumpers. A goat can stand on a narrow ledge and eat leaves that a cow cannot reach. This is why farmers keep goats on hills.

Horses are strong enough to pull a plough or a cart. A horse can hear a long way, and it remembers the way home in the dark.

Ducks have webbed feet, so they swim well and walk a little wobbly. A duck will raise her ducklings on her own, without any help.

Pigs are very clever with their noses. A pig can push a gate open that looks too heavy for it.

Dogs and cats have their own work. The dog barks to warn the farmer of strangers. The cat sleeps in the warm hay and keeps the mice away from the grain sacks.

And **bees** work hardest of all. One bee visits thousands of flowers in a day. A whole hive can make a pot of honey in a good season.
examples: Look, the cow is chewing the long grass.
The sheep has a very soft coat, just wool.
The duck has webbed feet, so she can swim.
sections.heading: The animals that live here

sections.body:
A farm is a wonderful place to visit, but the animals have not met you before. If you move too fast or make too much noise, they will be frightened. A frightened cow is not a friendly cow. So there is a way to do it.

First, wash your hands before you go. Farms carry germs that do not belong to us, and a farm dog may like to lick your fingers.

Second, stand outside the fence and look first. Let the animals come to you. Many farm animals are curious and will walk over to see you by themselves.

Third, ask the farmer before you touch. The farmer knows which animal is nervous and which one is happy to be stroked.

Fourth, move slowly and keep your voice soft. Horses hear far better than we do, and a loud shout makes a cow step backwards.

Fifth, wash your hands again when you leave. Then you can eat your lunch without thinking about it.
examples: May I pet the cow? I will wait for the farmer.
I will move slowly so that I do not frighten her.
I wash my hands before and after the visit.
sections.heading: How to visit a farm safely
steps: Wash your hands before you go.
Stand outside the fence and look first.
Ask the farmer before you touch an animal.
Move slowly and keep your voice soft.
Wash your hands again when you leave.

sections.body:
Farmers have their own words, and once you know them you can talk about a farm like the people who work there.

Livestock means the animals a farmer keeps on purpose. Cows, sheep, goats, pigs and chickens are all livestock.

A **barn** is the big farm building where the animals sleep and where the hay is stored. It is usually the safest, warmest place on the farm, and the animals go in when the weather turns cold.

Grazing means eating grass that is growing in a field. You can watch grazing from the road: the animals all move slowly in the same direction, nibbling as they go.

Fodder is the food we give to farm animals, such as hay, straw and root vegetables. It is not the same as the food we eat ourselves.

There are more words if you want them. **A lamb** is a young sheep, a **calf** is a young cow, and a **piglet** is a young pig. A **herd** is a group of cows, and a **flock** is a group of sheep or birds. A **stable** is the building where horses live.
examples: These cows are livestock, so the farmer milks them.
The hay is kept dry inside the barn.
The sheep are grazing, and they move as they eat.
sections.heading: The words farmers use every day

terms.example: Cows, sheep and goats are all livestock on this farm.

sections.body:
Most farm animals are gentle and well behaved. Still, they are big, and they do not know how strong they are. A horse that pulls a cart can pull a cart and a child too. A cow that is frightened can kick. A dog that is surprised can snap.

So remember three things. Do not go behind an animal, because it cannot see you there. Do not put your fingers through a fence, because the animal may bite to defend itself. And do not shout, because a frightened animal panics and runs.

If an animal does not want to be touched, that is the end of the meeting. Say thank you and walk away. The farmer will not mind at all.
examples: Please do not put your hand through the fence.
I will not walk behind the horse.
I am sorry, I did not know the cow was shy.
sections.heading: Animals can hurt you, even kind ones

sections.body:
The farmer is often awake before the sun. Here is an ordinary morning on an animal farm.

The first job is milking the cows. The farmer washes each cow, and the warm milk goes straight into the churn.

Then the hens are fed. The grain goes into the trough, and the hens come running so fast that they trip over each other. The farmer collects the eggs, and there is always one egg that is warmer than the rest, because that hen laid it just now.

After that the pigs are let out of their pen, and the goats are given fodder. The sheep are checked, because a sheep can walk away with a thorn in its foot without saying anything.

The horse gets his hay and his water. The fence is looked at, and any wire that is loose is tied again. A hole in a fence is a hole in the future, because everything on a farm eventually tries to walk out through it.

At midday the animals rest in the shade, and the farmer works in the field. In the evening, the eggs are collected again and the animals are let into the barn for the night. Then the dog walks around the yard one last time, and the farm goes quiet.
examples: The farmer milks the cows first thing in the morning.
The hens come running when the grain goes into the trough.
The dog walks around the yard before everyone goes to bed.
sections.heading: The work on a farm starts very early

item.summary: A farm is a busy place where animals live, work and eat. After reading this you can name the animals you will meet on a farm, use the words farmers use every day, and visit a farm without frightening anybody.
item.title: Meet the Animals on the Farm
